documents.title: SPA pack — Stock Purchase Agreement (Meridian Grid / Corvess Analytics) execution version
documents.body:
STOCK PURCHASE AGREEMENT — EXECUTION VERSION

This STOCK PURCHASE AGREEMENT (this "Agreement") is entered into as of March 12, 2026, by and among Meridian Grid Holdings, Inc., a Delaware corporation ("Buyer"), Talvane Energy Partners, LLC, a Texas limited liability company ("Seller"), and Corvess Analytics, Inc., a Delaware corporation (the "Company").

RECITALS

WHEREAS, Seller owns all 2,400,000 issued and outstanding shares of common stock, par value $0.001 per share, of the Company (the "Shares"); and WHEREAS, Seller desires to sell, and Buyer desires to purchase, all of the Shares upon the terms set forth herein.

ARTICLE II — PURCHASE AND SALE

Section 2.1 Purchase Price. The aggregate consideration payable by Buyer for the Shares shall be Eighty-Four Million Dollars ($84,000,000) (the "Base Purchase Price"), payable at Closing by wire transfer of immediately available funds, subject only to the working capital adjustment described in Section 2.4.

Section 2.2 Escrow. At the Closing, Buyer shall withhold from the Base Purchase Price and deposit with Sterling Fiduciary Trust Company, N.A. (the "Escrow Agent"): (a) Six Million Three Hundred Thousand Dollars ($6,300,000) (the "Indemnity Escrow Amount"), to be held in the Indemnity Escrow Account for eighteen (18) months following the Closing Date as the primary (but not exclusive) source of recovery for indemnification claims under Article VIII; and (b) One Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars ($1,500,000) (the "Adjustment Escrow Amount"), to be held in the Adjustment Escrow Account solely to secure the working capital adjustment under Section 2.4.

Section 2.3 No Contingent Consideration. For the avoidance of doubt, the Base Purchase Price is fixed, and no portion of the consideration payable hereunder is subject to any earn-out, milestone payment, royalty, revenue share, or other contingent payment obligation of any kind.

Section 2.4 Working Capital Adjustment. The Base Purchase Price shall be adjusted dollar-for-dollar to the extent Closing Working Capital deviates from the Target Working Capital of $9,750,000, in accordance with the procedures set forth on Exhibit C.

ARTICLE VII — CONDITIONS TO CLOSING

The obligations of Buyer to consummate the Closing are subject to: (a) the accuracy in all material respects of the representations and warranties of Seller and the Company; (b) the expiration or termination of any applicable waiting period under the HSR Act; (c) the absence of any Material Adverse Effect since the date hereof; (d) receipt of the Northgrid ISO interconnection consent; and (e) delivery of an officer's certificate, the executed Escrow Agreement, and resignations of each director of the Company.

ARTICLE VIII — INDEMNIFICATION

Section 8.1 Survival. The representations and warranties of Seller and the Company (other than the Fundamental Representations) shall survive the Closing for a period of eighteen (18) months following the Closing Date. The Fundamental Representations shall survive until sixty (60) days after the expiration of the applicable statute of limitations. Covenants shall survive in accordance with their terms.

Section 8.2 Cap. The aggregate liability of Seller for indemnification claims under Section 8.1(a) shall not exceed Twelve Million Six Hundred Thousand Dollars ($12,600,000) (the "Cap"); provided, that the Cap shall not apply to claims arising out of the Fundamental Representations or Fraud, which shall instead be capped at the Base Purchase Price.

Section 8.3 Basket. Seller shall have no liability under Section 8.1(a) unless and until the aggregate amount of all Losses exceeds Four Hundred Twenty Thousand Dollars ($420,000) (the "Deductible"), in which case Seller shall be liable only for Losses in excess of the Deductible. The Deductible operates as a true deductible and not as a tipping or first-dollar basket.

ARTICLE X — MISCELLANEOUS

Section 10.6 Governing Law; Jurisdiction. This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to its conflicts of law principles. Each party irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the Delaware Court of Chancery (or, if such court lacks jurisdiction, the federal courts located in Wilmington, Delaware).

documents.title: SPA pack — Stock Purchase Agreement (Halden Bay / Orlyn Foods) execution version
documents.body:
STOCK PURCHASE AGREEMENT — EXECUTION VERSION

This STOCK PURCHASE AGREEMENT (this "Agreement") is made as of April 3, 2026, by and among Halden Bay Capital Acquisition Corp., a Delaware corporation ("Buyer"), Renwick Orlyn Holdings LLC, a New York limited liability company ("Principal Seller"), the other holders listed on Schedule A (together with Principal Seller, the "Sellers"), and Orlyn Foods Group, Inc., a New York corporation (the "Company").

RECITALS

WHEREAS, the Sellers collectively own all 1,150,000 issued and outstanding shares of capital stock of the Company (the "Shares"); and WHEREAS, the Sellers desire to sell, and Buyer desires to purchase, all of the Shares.

ARTICLE II — PURCHASE AND SALE

Section 2.1 Base Purchase Price. The aggregate base consideration for the Shares shall be Fifty-Two Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars ($52,500,000) (the "Base Purchase Price"), payable at Closing as set forth in the Funds Flow Memorandum.

Section 2.2 Escrow. At the Closing, Buyer shall withhold from the Base Purchase Price and deposit Four Million Dollars ($4,000,000) (the "Indemnity Escrow Amount") with Lakemont Escrow Services LLC, as escrow agent, to be held in escrow for twelve (12) months following the Closing Date as the sole and exclusive source of recovery for indemnification claims under Section 9.1(a), other than claims based on Fraud.

Section 2.3 Earn-Out. In addition to the Base Purchase Price, Buyer shall pay to the Sellers contingent consideration of up to Ten Million Dollars ($10,000,000) (the "Earn-Out"), payable in accordance with Exhibit D if the Company's Net Revenue for the fiscal year ending December 31, 2027 equals or exceeds Sixty-One Million Dollars ($61,000,000). Fifty percent (50%) of the Earn-Out is payable at a Net Revenue threshold of $56,000,000, with straight-line interpolation between the thresholds.

ARTICLE VII — CONDITIONS TO CLOSING

Buyer's obligation to close is conditioned upon: (a) the accuracy of the Sellers' representations and warranties, subject to the Material Adverse Effect standard set forth in Section 7.2; (b) receipt of the consent of Brantley Cold Chain Logistics, Inc. under the Master Distribution Agreement; (c) payoff letters with respect to the Vantera Credit Facility; and (d) delivery of the executed Escrow Agreement, FIRPTA certificates, and the Restrictive Covenant Agreements of each Key Employee.

ARTICLE IX — INDEMNIFICATION

Section 9.1 Survival. The representations and warranties in Article IV and Article V (other than the Fundamental Representations) shall survive the Closing for twelve (12) months following the Closing Date, at which time they shall expire together with any right to assert a claim not previously noticed. The Fundamental Representations shall survive for six (6) years following the Closing Date.

Section 9.2 Cap. Except with respect to Fundamental Representations and Fraud, the aggregate liability of the Sellers under this Article IX shall not exceed Seven Million Eight Hundred Seventy-Five Thousand Dollars ($7,875,000) (the "Indemnity Cap").

Section 9.3 Basket. The Sellers shall not be liable under Section 9.1(a) unless the aggregate amount of Losses exceeds Two Hundred Sixty-Two Thousand Five Hundred Dollars ($262,500) (the "Threshold"), in which case the Sellers shall be liable for all such Losses from the first dollar, and not merely the excess. The Threshold is a tipping basket.

ARTICLE XI — MISCELLANEOUS

Section 11.4 Governing Law; Venue. This Agreement and all disputes arising hereunder shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of New York, without giving effect to any choice-of-law rules that would apply the law of another jurisdiction. The parties consent to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts sitting in New York County, New York, and waive any objection to venue therein.

Section 11.7 Transfer Taxes. All transfer, documentary, and stamp taxes shall be borne fifty percent (50%) by Buyer and fifty percent (50%) by the Sellers.

SECOND DRAFT — FOR DISCUSSION PURPOSES ONLY — SUPERSEDED BY EXECUTION VERSION — NOT FOR EXECUTION

[Drafting note (Whitlock & Farrow LLP, deal counsel to Talvane): this second-round draft dated February 20, 2026 reflects Seller's markup of Buyer's first draft. All economic terms below were subsequently renegotiated at the February 27 principals' call and DO NOT reflect the executed deal. Refer to the execution version circulated March 12, 2026 for the final deal points.]

STOCK PURCHASE AGREEMENT (DRAFT) by and among Meridian Grid Holdings, Inc. ("Buyer"), Talvane Energy Partners, LLC ("Seller"), and Corvess Analytics, Inc. (the "Company").

ARTICLE II — PURCHASE AND SALE (DRAFT TERMS)

Section 2.1 Purchase Price. The aggregate consideration for the Shares shall be Eighty Million Dollars ($80,000,000) (the "Base Purchase Price") [Seller note: Seller continues to seek $86,000,000; bracketed pending valuation call].

Section 2.2 Escrow. Buyer shall deposit Six Million Dollars ($6,000,000) as the Indemnity Escrow Amount [Buyer proposed 7.5% of the Base Purchase Price; Seller countered 6.0%] and One Million Dollars ($1,000,000) as the Adjustment Escrow Amount, in each case with an escrow agent to be agreed.

Section 2.3 [RESERVED — Buyer's first draft contained an earn-out of up to $5,000,000 tied to 2026 booked revenue; Seller rejected any contingent consideration and this concept was dropped from subsequent drafts.]

ARTICLE VIII — INDEMNIFICATION (DRAFT TERMS)

Section 8.1 Survival. Non-fundamental representations and warranties to survive for twenty-four (24) months following the Closing Date [Seller markup: reduce to 15 months; compromise to be discussed].

Section 8.2 Cap. Seller's aggregate indemnification liability not to exceed Twelve Million Dollars ($12,000,000) [Seller markup: 12% of Base Purchase Price].

Section 8.3 Basket. Deductible of Four Hundred Thousand Dollars ($400,000) [structure — deductible vs. tipping — still open in this draft].

ARTICLE X — MISCELLANEOUS (DRAFT)

Section 10.6 Governing Law. [Open issue in this draft: Buyer proposes Delaware; Seller's Texas-based tax counsel raised Texas law for the escrow agreement only. Resolved in favor of Delaware in the execution version.]

[End of superseded draft. Do not cite the figures above as deal points; they were superseded in their entirety.]

documents.title: SPA pack — Letter of Intent (Halden Bay / Orlyn Foods) non-binding term sheet
documents.body:
NON-BINDING LETTER OF INTENT

January 9, 2026

Board of Directors
Orlyn Foods Group, Inc.
41 Cortland Mill Road, Utica, New York

Re: Proposed acquisition of Orlyn Foods Group, Inc.

Ladies and Gentlemen:

This letter of intent (this "LOI") sets forth the principal indicative terms on which Halden Bay Capital Acquisition Corp. ("Halden Bay") proposes to acquire all of the outstanding capital stock of Orlyn Foods Group, Inc. (the "Company") from its shareholders. EXCEPT FOR THE EXCLUSIVITY AND CONFIDENTIALITY PROVISIONS IN PARAGRAPHS 7 AND 8, THIS LOI IS NON-BINDING AND DOES NOT CONSTITUTE AN OFFER, AND NO DEAL POINT BELOW IS FINAL UNTIL REFLECTED IN A DEFINITIVE EXECUTED STOCK PURCHASE AGREEMENT.

1. Purchase Price (indicative). An aggregate base purchase price of Fifty Million Dollars ($50,000,000), on a cash-free, debt-free basis, subject to confirmatory diligence, quality-of-earnings review, and customary working capital adjustment.

2. Escrow (indicative). An indemnity escrow equal to approximately seven percent (7%) of the base purchase price (approximately $3,500,000), held for a period to be negotiated between twelve (12) and eighteen (18) months.

3. Contingent Consideration (concept only). The parties will discuss an earn-out of up to Eight Million Dollars ($8,000,000) tied to fiscal 2027 performance metrics to be defined. Structure, thresholds, and caps remain entirely open.

4. Indemnification (indicative). Customary indemnification package with a cap in the range of 12–15% of the base purchase price and a basket in the range of 0.5% of the base purchase price; deductible-versus-tipping treatment to be negotiated.

5. Diligence and Timing. Halden Bay expects to complete diligence within 60 days, with a target signing in early April 2026.

6. Governing Documents. The definitive stock purchase agreement will supersede this LOI in all respects, and only the deal points stated in the executed agreement will govern.

7. Exclusivity. The Company grants Halden Bay exclusivity for 75 days from the date hereof.

8. Confidentiality. The parties reaffirm the mutual NDA dated November 18, 2025.

Very truly yours,
HALDEN BAY CAPITAL ACQUISITION CORP.
By: Marta Illesford, Managing Director

Agreed and acknowledged (as to Paragraphs 7 and 8 only):
ORLYN FOODS GROUP, INC.
By: Peter D. Renwick, Chief Executive Officer

documents.title: SPA pack — Deal team correspondence re escrow negotiation (Meridian Grid / Corvess Analytics)
documents.body:
FROM: Adrienne Kolvar, Whitlock & Farrow LLP (counsel to Talvane Energy Partners)
TO: Deal Team Distribution — Project Copperline
DATE: March 2, 2026
SUBJECT: RE: RE: Copperline — escrow sizing and structure (privileged & confidential)

Team —

Summarizing where we landed after this morning's call with Bryce Hollandale at Garnett Shale LLP (Meridian's counsel), so the record is in one place ahead of final drafting.

1. Escrow sizing history. Meridian opened at Seven Million Dollars ($7,000,000) for the indemnity escrow, citing the open Northgrid ISO consent and the unresolved sales tax exposure in the diligence memo. We countered at Five Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars ($5,500,000), pointing to the clean Q4 audit. On the principals' call, the CEOs agreed to split the difference at a number modestly north of six million; the precise figure is set out in Section 2.2 of the execution version and controls over anything in this thread. Do not quote figures from this email in the closing set — the executed agreement is the only source of truth for the deal points.

2. Structure. Two-account structure is agreed: a separate adjustment escrow (held only for the working capital true-up) alongside the indemnity escrow. Sterling Fiduciary Trust confirmed standard fee schedule; fees split 50/50.

3. Release mechanics. Indemnity escrow releases at the end of the survival period for non-fundamental reps, less any amounts subject to pending claim notices. Bryce agreed to drop the proposed 12-month interim partial release.

4. Open items for the closing checklist: (a) escrow agreement signature pages from Sterling; (b) wire instructions certificate; (c) confirm the adjustment escrow account number before the funds flow memo is finalized.

5. Note for the extraction team: when you populate the deal-point tracker, pull every number from the execution version circulated by Bryce on March 12 — not from this thread, not from the February drafts.

Best,
Adrienne

---

FROM: Bryce Hollandale, Garnett Shale LLP
SENT: March 2, 2026 11:41 AM
TO: Adrienne Kolvar; Deal Team Distribution — Project Copperline
SUBJECT: RE: Copperline — escrow sizing and structure

Adrienne — confirmed on all points. We will circulate the conformed execution version once the schedules are locked. Please make sure your side's tracker reflects the executed Section 2.2 figures rather than the bracketed draft numbers.

— Bryce
